title: Close-up of stacked green circuit boards with ribbon connectors
objects_and_counts: Two small green daughterboards are mounted side-by-side on a larger green main PCB; each daughterboard has one visible square black integrated-circuit package (two ICs total visible).
A larger green main PCB is visible beneath the daughterboards with multiple rows of through-hole pin headers; at least one long double-row pin header is visible along the near edge.

Six white plastic wire-to-board connectors (JST-style) are visible along the top edge of the daughterboards, each with an attached pink-and-white flat ribbon cable; several of these connector bodies are partially cropped at the top edge of the image.
One multicolour (rainbow) flat ribbon cable is visible entering the scene from the left and routing behind the daughterboards.
One small blue rectangular module or sensor pack with a white label is visible at lower left, sitting on a tan or cardboard surface; the module appears to be separate from the stacked PCBs.
Multiple small surface-mount passive components (capacitors/resistors) and through-hole connectors visible on the PCBs; these are numerous and not counted individually.
No people are visible in the photographed scene and there are no posters or screens that show people.
spatial_relations: Two daughterboards are mounted adjacent to each other on top of the larger main PCB, occupying the upper-center portion of the image.

The six white JST-style connectors are arranged in a roughly horizontal row along the top edge of the daughterboards, with pink-and-white flat cables plugged into them and extending upward out of frame.
A multicolour ribbon cable approaches from the left and passes behind the stacked PCBs toward the upper-left quadrant of the image.
The blue rectangular module sits to the lower left of the stacked PCBs, resting on a tan/cardboard surface beneath the edge of the main board.
A long double-row pin header runs along the near (bottom) edge of the main PCB, parallel to the front edge of the image.
colours_and_materials: PCBs are green with visible white silkscreen text and markings.
Wire-to-board connectors are white plastic with pink-and-white flat ribbon cables attached.
A multicolour (rainbow) ribbon cable includes red, orange, yellow, green, blue and purple conductors.
A small module is housed in blue plastic with a white label and blue printed logo or mark.
Pin headers and many connector pins are metallic (soldered/tinned appearance).
uncertainties: Exact room name or number is not visible anywhere in the image; location cannot be determined from the image.

Some small silkscreen labels and pin labels on the PCB are partially obscured or out of focus and not fully legible; I transcribed 'COMMUNICATION', 'DIGITAL', 'RX0 TX0', and 'SCL' where they appear readable, and used [unreadable] for other label fragments.

The precise count of small surface-mount components and individual header pins is not given because components overlap and some are out of focus; counts above are for clearly distinguishable whole items only.
The white label on the blue rectangular module contains diagrammatic printing and text that is partly blurred; its full text could not be transcribed reliably.
Some of the white JST-style connector bodies are cropped at the image top edge, so the visible count (six) is a lower bound for connectors present at that edge of the assembly.
